finding.title: Hold expiry lives in a timer in the web process
finding.explanation: placeHold releases the hold from a `setTimeout` in the process that served the request. A deploy, a crash or a scale-down drops the timer, and the slot stays held with nobody paying for it. The hold row has `expiresAt`, but nothing reads it.
finding.reasoningSummary: No job, cron or query reads hold.expiresAt (search_code). The web processes restart on every deploy (deploy/web.yaml rolls them), several times a day.
finding.suggestedFix: Release expired holds from the worker: a scheduled job that releases every hold whose expiresAt has passed, and drop the timer.

evidence.text: search_code "expiresAt": 2 matches, both writes; no reader in src/ or jobs/
